stem: A student council at a university in Lahore wants to estimate the percent of the university's 9,000 students who use the library's mobile app. Which of the following methods is most likely to produce a sample that represents all of the university's students?

choices.A: Survey 300 students who are studying inside the library on one afternoon.
choices.B: Post a poll on the app and record the first 300 responses.
choices.C: Select 300 students at random from the registrar's list of all students, and survey them.
choices.D: Survey the first 300 students who arrive at the main gate on Monday morning.

solution: A representative sample gives every student the same chance of being selected.
Selecting students at random from a complete list does this; the other methods favor certain students.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Students inside the library are more likely to use the library's app, so this sample over-represents users.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Only app users can see a poll on the app, so this sample includes only users.
explanation.C: Correct. A random sample from a list of all students is likely to represent the whole university.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Early arrivals at one gate are a convenience sample and may differ from other students.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'D'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
methods = {'A': 'convenience', 'B': 'voluntary', 'C': 'random', 'D': 'convenience'}
ok = [k for k, v in methods.items() if v == 'random']
assert ok == [answer]
assert 'at random' in choices[answer] and 'all students' in choices[answer]
